blocks.text: Good morning Jennifer,

Thank you for the note, and for the time on the call last week. That conversation settled which audience we lead with, and it has already sharpened the first set of core messages for {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}}. Amy Carter has the draft in hand and will work your marks in as they come.

The next piece is the round of short interviews with your executives, so the language sits on how they actually speak rather than on our guess at it. Before I propose times, it would help to know which two or three people you would like us to sit with, and roughly when they tend to be free over the coming fortnight.

Send me the names and I will come back the same day with a few windows that fit their diaries. For the file, sign-off on the Suarez-Jones messaging stays with you, Jennifer Herrera, so nothing firms up without your word.
Regards
Jennifer,

Following John Macias's note, I wanted to close the loop on the draft itself. The revised first set of core messages for {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} is ready on our side, and I will send it in a form you can mark up directly, with the two or three lines that turn on the audience question flagged so they are easy to find.

So the interviews and the draft do not cross, I have held the executive language loosely where I expect their own words to change it. If you can point me to the people John will be sitting with, I will make sure the questions we bring line up with the messages the Suarez-Jones executives will end up carrying.

I will get the marked draft to you this week either way. If reading it cold is awkward, a short call works just as well, and I will set one up around your schedule. For our file, final sign-off on the wording stays with you, Jennifer Herrera.
Regards
Good morning Jennifer,

Thank you, that helps. Between your note and Amy Carter's, I think we have what we need to move. The names you sent let me shape the interviews for {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} around the people whose voice carries the message furthest, and Amy's marked draft will reach you this week to read alongside them.

On the short call Amy raised, I think it is worth doing ahead of the interviews, so we walk in aligned. If a half hour early next week suits you, tell me which day sits best and I will build everything else around it.
I will send three interview windows for each of your executives by tomorrow and hold them for your word. Nothing on the Suarez-Jones side is booked until you confirm, Jennifer Herrera.
Regards
Jennifer,

The marked draft of the first set of core messages for {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}} is on its way to you now, a little ahead of where I promised. As I mentioned, the lines that shift with the audience question are flagged in the margin, so you can go straight to the two or three that will matter most.

I have left room in the wording for what John Macias hears in the interviews, so please read it as a working draft and not a finished one. If anything reads false to how your leadership actually speaks, mark it freely; that is the most useful thing you can send back.

For our record, final sign-off stays with you, Jennifer Herrera. Send it over with your notes whenever it suits, and I will turn them the same day so the Suarez-Jones messaging is ready before the interviews begin.
Regards

blocks.text: What we covered

We met to take stock of the executive messaging work at its midpoint and to agree what carries us through the coming weeks. The room was small and the conversation direct, which is how this engagement has run from the start.

John Macias reported that the round of executive interviews is complete. He walked us through what the leadership's own language had changed, and two of the core messages have already been reshaped around how the executives actually speak. The group agreed the set now sits closer to the company's own voice, which was the whole point of the exercise.

Jennifer Herrera then took us through her team's marks on the first set. Most were small matters of tone, but two touched the investor-facing line we had flagged at the outset. We talked through how to hold the meaning while easing the claim, and settled on wording in the room. I will circulate that wording for a final read before it is fixed.

We also looked ahead to the client-facing materials that will carry the messages outward. Those are still early by design. We agreed to keep them light until the core set is locked, so the finished pieces are built once rather than remade around a late change.

On cadence, we agreed the current rhythm is working: short notes tied to the piece of work they concern, a standing thread for the messaging, and a working session like this one when a decision needs the whole group in a room. Jennifer Herrera asked that we keep her copied on anything that touches timing, and we will.
Where we landed

The core messages are close to final, pending the last read on the two reworked lines. The materials wait on that lock. We set the next checkpoint as a working review of the refined set with the wider Suarez-Jones leadership, ahead of any further build.

We noted one open risk, and it is a mild one. The investor-facing lines are the most likely to draw a late change, so we are holding a little room for one more pass on them before the set is fixed. Nothing about the timeline concerns us at this point.
Actions

rows: Circulate the agreed wording on the two investor-facing lines for a final read

Confirm the attendees for the leadership review

blocks.text: Status Report
Engagement: Executive Messaging for {{fact:f:E-2023-001.client}}. Prepared by John Macias.
Where the work stands

We are roughly at the midpoint of the engagement, and the work is on track. The core messages are drafted, tested against the leadership's own words, and close to final. Both sides are pulling the same way, and the correspondence has stayed clean, which is what keeps a job like this from drifting.

The short version is that the hard part, agreeing what the company should say and in what voice, is largely behind us. What remains is to lock the wording and build the materials that carry it. That is the steadier half of the work.

On the commercials, the engagement runs on a fixed fee of {{fact:f:E-2023-001.fee}}, and we are tracking within it. A little under half of the fee is committed against the work done to date. That is where we would want to be at this stage, with the more predictable phase still ahead of us.
Since the last report

We completed the round of executive interviews and used them to sharpen the core set. Two of the messages changed in a real way once we heard how the leadership actually speaks. Both are stronger for it, and both read now as the company's own rather than ours.

Amy Carter took your team's marks on the first set and reworked the investor-facing lines, holding the meaning while easing the claims that felt a shade too firm. We reviewed the refined set with the Suarez-Jones leadership at our last working session, and the feedback was light. We settled the two lines that mattered most in the room.

The review itself was a good sign. Your leadership pushed on exactly the lines we expected them to push on, and left the rest largely alone. When a client's marks land where you thought they would, it usually means the underlying account is sound, and we took it that way.

We have also opened the client-facing materials that will carry the messages outward. Those are early and deliberately so. We are keeping them light until the core set is locked, so nothing has to be remade around a late change to the wording.

On our side, Amy Carter has kept the correspondence and the version history in order throughout, so the current draft is always the one you are reading and nothing lives only in an inbox. It is unglamorous work, and it is the reason a job this heavy on email has stayed legible.
The weeks ahead
The immediate step is to lock the core messages. One round of marks is outstanding, and once those are in, the set is final. Amy Carter and I can close that out the same week the marks come back.

From there we build the materials in earnest and prepare your executives to carry the language into their own conversations, the announcements and investor briefings where it has to hold. I expect this half of the engagement to move at a steadier pace than the first, now that the foundation is set.

In practical terms, the coming weeks will hold less of the open-ended work of the first half and more of the concrete: a fixed set of messages, a defined set of materials, and a plan to hand the language to the people who will speak it. We will keep the same cadence of short notes tied to each piece, so you can follow the work without having to ask where it stands.
What I am watching

Two things, both small. The investor-facing lines are the most likely to draw a late change, so I am keeping room for one more pass on them before we fix the set. And because the materials depend on a locked core set, any slip on the wording will push the build behind it. Neither worries me at this point. I am simply keeping an eye on both.

The one thing I need from your side is the final round of marks on the refined messages. Send those back whenever they are ready, and we will lock the set within the week. I will send the next report at the three-quarter mark, or sooner if anything of note moves before then.
